title: First Punic War (264–241 BCE)
key_facts: Naval conflict between Rome and Carthage primarily over control of Sicily
Rome built a navy and innovated with the corvus boarding device
Ended with Roman victory and Carthaginian evacuation of Sicily
causes: Rivalry over influence in Sicily (Messana) and trade routes
Allied entanglements drawing Rome and Carthage into war
outcome: Treaty compelled Carthage to cede Sicily and pay indemnities
Rome emerged as a naval power
impacts: Roman expansion beyond the Italian peninsula
Set stage for renewed conflicts (Second Punic War)
